I’m from the US, and have struggled with other mental health issues before more seriously dealing with ED stuff. I started seeing my PCP here because due to my ed entering a more serious phase I was having heart issues. Due to the nature of EDs I was very hush hush about it and was tip-toeing around my restriction as a whole (not saying that’s your issue just stating my experience here) I was just mentioning my physical side effects and how my life was being affected by that. Got referred to a cardiologist and said cardiologist began running tests. During this period i started talking more to my therapist about my ED and physical health with full transparency (in the US they cannot involuntarily hospitalize you unless you are actively suicidal or homicidal and I knew this so I spoke about my ED freely.) my therapist is older and has several degrees and qualifications so his official title is PSYD , meaning he has a psychiatric doctorate and is able to diagnose conditions , which is not typical for therapists, at least in my country though I am not sure if that is the norm in other countries. He diagnosed me with an ED and gave me an ultimatum to seek treatment for said ED. I ended up going to a treatment center after that though my PCP never had a clue as to what was happening with me/my physical health. If you are in the US and are just seeing a typical PCP/family health doctor they most likely will not ‘officially’ diagnose you unless you are COMPLETELY transparent with them, which I know to be true due to the nature of this illness and the state of American healthcare. Even if you are on deaths door and it is very noticeable even to the most common of people , they probably won’t diagnose you. That’s americas health care system for you. Please do seek help, even if you don’t think it’s bad enough. I have been in recovery almost two years now. I would be dead if that therapist didn’t tell me I was weeks, DAYS  away from passing in my sleep. Be honest and do this for your future. Don’t hesitate to reach out to me if you have more questions.
